newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes ease as traders wait for July.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes ease as traders wait for July.

text.p: Crude oil prices on the U.S. West Coast dropped Thursday, with business quiet as traders shifted their focus from June to July barrels.
"It's the usual lull," said one trader, referring to lack of trade at the end of the month.

As pipeline scheduling finished up last week, traders said ARCO sold 2,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of Line 63 blended crude to Paramount Refinery. The parcel was priced at $3.50 under July WTI, traders said.

Meanwhile, regional benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude has been declining steadily relative to U.S. benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) for nearly three months after peaking in early March at an 80 cent discount to WTI.
Last Friday BP America sold a cargo to Texaco Transport and Trading at a discount of $1.75, and offered it this week at minus $1.60.
Buyers expected the next cargo to sell at $1.90-$2.00 off July WTI.
Crude prices, already pressured by South American grades, could come under more pressure if Canadian imports increased by mid-summer as anticipated.
Heavier valley crudes were seeing flat or easier differentials to posted prices, which were lowered on Tuesday by between 25 and 50 cents, traders said.
